discussion: Add the allow_no_value API note that valueless options cannot start multiline values and that an indented continuation raises MultilineContinuationError, while options with values can still use multiline continuations; then check the patched candidate.

operation.new:
>>> # Settings without values provide None:
     >>> config["mysqld"]["skip-bdb"]

     >>> # Settings which aren't specified still raise an error:
     >>> config["mysqld"]["does-not-exist"]
     Traceback (most recent call last):
       ...
     KeyError: 'does-not-exist'

  A valueless option cannot start a multiline value.  If an indented
  continuation line follows such an option, the parser raises
  :exc:`MultilineContinuationError`, a subclass of :exc:`ParsingError`,
  exposing the parsing source, the one-based line number of the offending
  continuation line and the exact offending line.  Indented continuation
  lines after an option that already has a value on its option line remain
  valid multiline values.

* *delimiters*, default value: ``('=', ':')``
operation.old:
>>> # Settings without values provide None:
     >>> config["mysqld"]["skip-bdb"]

     >>> # Settings which aren't specified still raise an error:
     >>> config["mysqld"]["does-not-exist"]
     Traceback (most recent call last):
       ...
     KeyError: 'does-not-exist'

* *delimiters*, default value: ``('=', ':')``
